title: eval-harness: add quality-gating CI hook for prompt-set regression checks
author: Priya Shah
description: This PR introduces a CI-level quality-gating hook that runs the eval-harness prompt-set regression checks as part of pre-merge verification. Motivation: prevent regressions in generation quality caused by model, prompt, or infra changes by blocking merges when key eval metrics drop beyond configured thresholds. The hook is configurable per-repo and per-branch and integrates with our existing CI (GitHub Actions) + comment/status reporting. Changes include a new GH Actions workflow, a lightweight CI hook library in the eval-harness package, default gating thresholds for primary prompt-sets, and docs for repository owners to opt-in or tune gates. Summary of behavior: - On PR open / update the workflow runs a targeted eval-harness job (quick mode) that evaluates configured prompt-sets using the PR head model/config. - The job publishes structured metrics and compares against stored baselines; if any metric falls below the gate threshold (absolute or relative delta) the job sets a failing check and adds an informative comment with traces and links to the full eval artifact. - Owners can mark gates as warning-only or set per-prompt tolerances via .eval/config.yaml. - The workflow is throttled and runs in quick mode by default to limit CI cost; full nightly runs remain in the eval-harness repo. Checklist: - [x] CI workflow .github/workflows/eval-harness-ci.yml - [x] eval-harness hook library: eval-harness/ci/hooks.py - [x] default gates config: eval-harness/config/quality_gates.yaml - [x] docs: docs/ci/eval-gating.md - [x] unit tests for hook logic - [x] end-to-end smoke run on canary repo Implementation notes: - The hook executes the harness in "quick" mode (smaller sample sizes, precompiled prompt bundles) with deterministic seeds to reduce flakiness. - Baselines are stored as artifacts in the eval-harness S3 bucket and referenced by gate IDs. - For ephemeral model variants (e.g., quantized/lightweight fallbacks) the hook compares against compatible baselines to avoid false positives. - To reduce noise, gates use a two-step threshold: absolute minimum + allowed relative degradation. See config file for defaults. Rollout plan: - Enable as opt-in on a few high-traffic repos for one week - Monitor false positive rate and CI cost (console dashboard) - Flip opt-in to opt-out after stabilization Notes on CI cost: the quick-mode run costs ~20% of a full eval and is designed to complete within the PR timeout budget. The workflow will auto-cancel prior runs on update to avoid duplicates.

release_notes: Adds an opt-in CI quality-gating hook that blocks merges when eval-harness prompt-set metrics regress beyond configured thresholds. Includes GH Actions workflow, hook library, default gate configs, and docs. Admins can tune gates via eval-harness/config/quality_gates.yaml.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the eval run quick to limit CI cost; teams can opt into full runs via repo-level config.
Baseline artifacts are managed in the eval-harness S3 bucket; has IAM scope restricted to CI service principal.
We expect initial onboarding to generate some noise; monitoring dashboards are added to the console to track false positives.
